subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Know the rules for writing good e-mails
Find the rules that are broken in e-mails
Plan an informal e-mail with the correct layout

tf.s: You should include a subject line in an e-mail.
tf.why: Yes! A subject line tells the reader what the e-mail is about.

tf.s: You should always use smileys in every e-mail.
tf.why: Use smileys only in the most informal e-mails.

tf.s: Writing in CAPITALS can make the reader think you are shouting.
tf.why: Right! Avoid writing whole words in capitals.

tf.s: E-mails are private, so it is safe to send a password.
tf.why: E-mails are not private; don't send confidential information.

tf.s: A good e-mail uses short sentences in one or two paragraphs.
tf.why: Correct! Keep e-mails short and clear.

tf.s: If a message is really urgent, it is better to use the telephone.
tf.why: Good! A phone call is faster for urgent messages.

tf.s: 'Take care, speak soon' is used at the beginning of an e-mail.
tf.why: It is a closing phrase, so it goes at the end.
Yes, it is friendly and informal.

tf.s: In an e-mail, the closing comes before the greeting.
tf.why: The greeting comes first, after the subject line.

tf.s: It is fine to write unkind things about other people in an e-mail.
tf.why: Think carefully about what you write; be polite.

mcq.q: Which rule says to keep e-mails short?
o: Use short sentences in one or two paragraphs
mcq.why: Short e-mails are easier to read.

mcq.q: What is missing from many of the e-mails with mistakes?
o: a subject line and correct punctuation
mcq.why: Good e-mails have a subject line and correct punctuation.

mcq.q: Which are parts of an e-mail?
o: subject line, greeting, body and closing
mcq.why: These parts make a clear e-mail layout.

mcq.q: Choose the best polite rewrite of 'PLEASE send me the MONEY'.
o: Could you please send the payment?
mcq.why: Polite language and normal letters are better.

mcq.q: You are planning an informal e-mail to a friend. Which plan is best?
mcq.why: An e-mail has a clear beginning, middle and end.
